Thanks for taking the time today - a quick recap and proposed next steps from our side. High level: AtlasHealth is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference of clinical summarization and triage models. Main decision points are GPU type, reserved capacity size, and whether we can meet your unit economics target.

Call notes / confirms: 
- Monthly token volume (combined input+output): approx 1.8B tokens/mo (Justin: "~1.8B, likely +/- 20% as usage grows")
- Target unit economics: $250-200 per 1M tokens (customer target range stated on call)
- Budget range: $150k-450k/mo (early estimate tied to capacity commit)
- Latency SLO: median <150ms, p95 <300ms for production flows
- Throughput: expected steady-state throughput ~600-800 concurrent end-user requests; peak bursts up to 1.2k concurrent. Equivalent target tokens/sec at peak ~8k-12k (depends on avg tokens per request).
- Model stack: mixture of instruction-tuned open models + custom fine-tuned heads (we discussed H100 vs A100 / 80GB and quantized variants).

Open questions we promised to follow up on: 
1) Recommended GPU type and sizing for 1.8B tokens/mo with your latency targets (Marcus to propose).
2) Rough cost math mapping reserved capacity pricing -> $/1M tokens so you can validate against your $250-200 target.
3) Proposal next steps: draft quote + SOW and a canary rollout plan for the first 30 days.

Attachments: I attached a capacity/pricing worksheet and a proposal template that we can populate after we confirm GPU sizing.

Next steps suggested: 
- Marcus to send technical sizing + throughput estimates (by EOD Wed).
- Neha to share pricing worksheet pre-populated with a baseline A100 and H100 scenario.
- Justin to confirm legal contact and preferred timeline for PO/commitment (Justin: said legal is "Elena; she handles procurement").

If any of the bullets above are off, flag and I'll update. Otherwise we'll aim to get the sizing & back-of-envelope cost to you by mid-week.

Justin / team - quick technical sizing and rough cost mapping based on the call. This is a back-of-envelope; if we move forward we'll run a short benchmark with your model artifacts.

Assumptions: 
- Avg tokens/request: triage=150, summarization=600; split of traffic ~80% triage / 20% summarization.
- Peak combined tokens/sec target: 10k (from Justin).

Sizing scenarios (throughput numbers are approximate sustained tokens/sec):
- 4x A100 80GB (quantized + aggressive batching): ~6k-8k tokens/sec sustained; good for <10k peak with some queueing. Latency p95 may hit ~300ms on summarization heavy bursts.
- 4x H100 80GB: ~10k-14k tokens/sec sustained; p95 latency comfortably <300ms with target batching.
- 8x A100 (burst/peak): baseline 12k-16k tokens/sec but higher cost and more ops overhead.

Recommendation: Given your target p95 and 10k peak tokens/sec, the conservative path is 4x H100 reserved, with an autoscaling/burst policy to add A100 capacity if needed. If budget is constrained, start with 4x A100 + aggressive quantization and a canary to validate latency - we can commit to an SLA-based fallback if performance degrades.

Cost math (very rough): 
- Input: reserved monthly GPU + infra + licensing approx. (example numbers for illustration only)
  - 4x A100 reserved: $120k/mo base (infra + ops + licensing) -> maps to ~$400-450 per 1M tokens at 1.8B tokens/mo
  - 4x H100 reserved: $190k/mo base -> maps to ~$250-320 per 1M tokens at 1.8B tokens/mo
  - 8x A100 reserved: $220k/mo base -> maps to ~$120-3200 per 1M tokens at higher throughput (but higher commit)

Notes: mapping cost->$/1M tokens changes with utilization. The H100 scenario is more cost-efficient per token at higher throughput because of better kernels and fewer nodes for KV cache. The A100 scenario can meet budget targets if utilization is high and customers accept slightly higher p95 latency or we use burst pooling.

Next steps from SE: 
- If you confirm model artifacts (or a representative model), we'll run a 24-48h perf benchmark on A100 and H100 to produce a validated cost/$1M tokens number.
- I'll populate the pricing worksheet with the three scenarios (attached) and call out the assumptions.

Happy to jump on another call to walk through the numbers.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
